title: PairGraph: An Efficient Search-space-aware Accelerator for High-performance Concurrent Pairwise Queries
problem: Concurrent pairwise queries on graphs suffer from irregular memory access patterns and poor data sharing due to low temporal/spatial locality when multiple query paths traverse overlapping graph structures.
motivation: Pairwise graph queries are widely used but processors struggle with concurrent query processing due to traversal irregularity; exploiting query search-space similarity can dramatically reduce memory pressure and improve throughput.
method: PairGraph employs a Search-space-aware Processing Model that identifies graph topology data traversed by multiple queries, identifies strong similarities in query search spaces concentrated on the topology between source-destination pairs, and reuses this shared data to minimize off-chip communications.
key_novelty: Search-space-aware processing model that exploits the strong similarity of concurrent query search spaces to maximize data reuse and minimize off-chip bandwidth.
contributions: Search-space-aware Processing Model identifying traversal similarities across concurrent pairwise queries
Accelerator design achieving 5.59-14.25x speedup over CPU Gemini and 3.76-7.58x over GPU Gunrock
1.67-4.28x speedup over cutting-edge accelerators LCCG, ScalaGraph, and ReGraph

metrics.speedup: 5.59-14.25x vs CPU; 3.76-7.58x vs GPU; 1.67-4.28x vs accelerators

limitations: Power consumption, area, and scalability to larger graph sizes not discussed.
primary_theme: Search-space-aware graph accelerator for concurrent pairwise queries
